form.notes: Form-associated like a native `<select multiple>`: one `FormData` entry per chosen value under `name` (repeated names), nothing submitted when nothing is chosen; resets to the `value` attribute, restores on navigation, joins <fieldset disabled>. `required` needs at least one value (valueMissing).

differences.text: Uncontrolled by default (D-006): `values` is the array and `value` the same list as whitespace-separated text (also the `value` attribute, the form reset default); a value that contains whitespace can only be set through `values`. `input` then `change` fire once per user toggle, select-all or clear; upstream is a controlled `value: string[]` with `onChange`.

Form-associated like a native `<select multiple>`: one entry per chosen value under `name` (repeated names in `FormData`), nothing chosen submits nothing; `required` needs at least one value. The restore state is the list of values.

The `is*` props are bare boolean attributes, `htmlName` is `name`, `isDefaultOpen` is the `open` attribute, `xstyle` and `data-testid` are replaced by class, style, `::part()` and host attributes; `has-clear` clears every value and fires the cancelable `tct-clear` first.
The checkbox marks are drawn by the shipped checkbox indicator element only (see SELECTOR-04); the popup opens below the trigger unless `placement="overlay"` (SELECTOR-05).

Every selection change is announced once and politely ("3 of 12 selected", "All selected", "Selection cleared"), and the select-all row is named for its state with a partial (mixed) state while some of the shown options are chosen. Async option states behave as for the selector (SELECTOR-06).

The opening keys highlight the first option (ArrowUp the last) since there is no single chosen row; Home, End and the Page keys, Escape, Tab and typeahead follow the selector contract (SELECTOR-07, SELECTOR-08).
As the selector (SELECTOR-09); the `badges` display uses `tct-badge` neutral badges with a "+N" overflow marker.
